The ITER switched coil-supply model (iter-switched-terminal-transients) predicts how stray inductances and coil capacitances shape the switching transients at the coil terminals, but ITER has no measured transients to check it against. JT-60SA has real pulses, and its coils are built like ITER's: NbTi cable-in-conduit, pancake-wound EF and CS coils. The lead decided on 14 October 2026 to replay real JT-60SA pulses through the same model, to observe the strays on a smaller machine of similar construction.

There is a lead in hand. The booster work found a step of nearly 180° between the 12f and the 18f–30f line phases on the 2021 idle windows, the signature of a second-order resonance in the coil loop between 12f and 18f (booster-converter-model §14). Its best single-resonance fit, 936 Hz at zero damping, is not confirmed: it still misses per window, by 48° at E100318's 30f, and the step survived §21's re-score. The resonance needs 6.4 to 14.6 µF at the coil terminals against a documented 0.6 µF screen. Distributed winding capacitance, which the ITER work found puts PF-coil resonances inside the converter band, is a candidate this plan can test.

The replay is an independent time-domain check (lead decision, relayed by the coil-circuit plan's owner). jt60sa-coil-circuit-model §6 keeps its frequency-domain sources; neither plan depends on the other until the switched sources are validated on a 2021 pulse. The work of the other JT-60SA plans is read, never edited. Results that bear on booster §14, §5 or §23 go to that plan's owner as messages.

§1 — What a replay can use and can observe

A discovery node inventoried what the replay can use, from local holdings and the knowledge graph while the site link was down (jt60sa-switched-replay-inputs):

  • 56 pulse archives, 27 of them 2021 coil-only commissioning pulses;
  • every stored channel at 4 kHz, with no faster PF recorder found;
  • the EF and CS winding geometry with document pages, but not the insulation thickness and material or the terminal and feeder construction;
  • nova's OP2 description, with 12 active coils and 155 passive filaments;
  • no shot-matched 2023 equilibrium held locally.

At 4 kHz the replay sees the lines to 2 kHz and the 12f–18f band, not the commutation edges. The section closes when that record lands. The site-only items move to the queries in §3 and §6, which run one shot at a time after the booster plan's own fetch.

§2 — The JT-60SA converters as switched circuits

The JT-60SA supplies are built from the same builders as the ITER units (src/power_convertor/converter_units.py), and their description has one owner, which the builders read rather than restate. src/power_convertor/configurations.py holds the booster's 30° series pair (_booster) and the base (_base), which for EF5 and EF2 is the CEA four-module base in circulating mode (phase groups 0, −30, 15 and −15°, current directions +, +, −, −); the ENEA base belongs to EF6. Its ConverterConfiguration.build returns the frequency-domain BridgePair, which SupplyModel composes. The switched units run on the existing solver, switched_circuit.Circuit.simulate; no new integrator is built. coil_system.py (_rating) holds the per-coil current and voltage limits. The frozen 2021 values come from fitted_parameters.py, which covers EF5 and EF2 only; §22's positive-current branch is a candidate, not frozen. The owner covers EF5, EF2 and EF6, with EF6 report-only because its filter state is undocumented, and it has no EF1 configuration, so this section builds EF5 and EF2. Extending to EF6 and EF1 means extending configurations.py and fitted_parameters.py first, as a node of its own. The node also replaces §1's inventory script's own trace reading with signals.load and FS_JT60SA, and adds a committed absent-channel test, both carried from §1's review. The 2023 ripple filter and both groundings come from filter_network.py. The units are fired from the recorded references (PSSCfst/refvol<coil>Bst and …Bse).

Done when two things hold. First, a unit fired from a 2021 idle window's references reproduces the frequency-domain booster model's lines (BridgePair, SupplyModel) at that operating point to a stated tolerance, with every parameter cited to its owner. Second, the inventory script reads traces through signals.load, and a committed test fails if a missing channel comes back as zeros. Negative control: dropping the booster pair's 30° shift brings up the 6f and 18f lines the frequency-domain model predicts.

§3 — The JT-60SA coil windings and their strays

Each EF and CS coil becomes sectioned windings through src/power_convertor/coil_windings.py, with the JT-60SA geometry from §1's record. That module classifies a coil by its ITER name today: an EF coil falls to a single section, a JT-60SA CS coil inherits the ITER CS pancake layers, and the dielectric constants are keyed on a PF prefix, with no error on an unknown name. This section extends it with machine-aware geometry: JT-60SA's EF and CS pancake structure from §1's record, dielectric values per machine, and a refusal for any coil name the geometry does not know. The insulation thickness and material and the terminal and feeder construction are not in anything held. They are asked for from the site documents in one bounded query (the wiki's coil and feeder documents through ssh jt-60sa, one at a time); until they arrive they are carried as ranges, marked assumed. The documented 0.6 µF screen and the base supply's per-bridge DC reactors (Plant Integration Document pp. 139–141) enter as circuit elements.

Done when each coil's terminal impedance from 0.1 Hz to 10 kHz is computed with its resonances marked, and the capacitance a 12f–18f resonance would need is set against what the windings, screen and reactors provide. Negative control: zero capacitance gives the bare inductive impedance.

§4 — The JT-60SA coupled plant from nova

The coils, the passive structure and the plasma couple through nova's narrow imported call, with the OP2 machine description. For the 2021 coil-only pulses the plasma source is empty, a vacuum case; for 2023 it is a reconstructed equilibrium (§6). The coupling-circuit plan's §5 already showed nova's OP2 passive structure predicting 8 of 9 measured coil-pair transfers within 4 to 8 % of M/L (EF1 to EF6 is 18.8 % off and open); that is the check on the plant. The section is held by gate g-jspr-1 on nova's call.

Done when the call returns the OP2 plant and its coil-pair transfer functions reproduce the coupling-circuit plan's measured ratios at 6f, 12f and 18f (data/jt60sa/coupling_transfer.json) within that plan's stated band. Negative control: with the passive structure removed from the plant, the coil-pair ratios leave that band at the frequencies where the structure screens, so the comparison is shown to discriminate.

§5 — The 2021 coil-only pulses, replayed

The switched units (§2) drive the sectioned coils (§3) in the coupled plant (§4) along recorded 2021 pulses, integrated by the existing solver, switched_circuit.Circuit.simulate, in the order §1 recommends:

  • E100310 on EF5, with E100303 as the base-supply control;
  • E100318 on EF5;
  • E100321 and E100324 on EF2.

EF6 and EF1 follow only once §2's owner extension covers them.

E100340 and E100317 are excluded as clean cases. The simulated coil voltage passes through the same measurement chain as the data (src/power_convertor/measurement.py, including the 104.6 µs interleave skew) before its lines from 6f to 30f are compared in amplitude and phase with the measured ones. The comparison reuses the scoring owner, prediction.py (score_case and line_result), which implements filter-grounding-prediction §1's amplitude, fold and phase bands. Two cautions from the coupling-circuit plan's owner apply: the coil-voltage channels shift by up to 28 V once a supply energises, so references are taken inside the window's own supply state, and current changes are read from the slow part of the current.

The question this section answers is whether the sectioned windings' capacitance, with the screen and the reactors, reproduces the 12f–18f phase step. The strays are then bounded from the 2021 data. With 4 kHz data only the response below 2 kHz is identifiable, and the record says which strays that constrains and which it cannot.

Done when the replay's line amplitudes and phases are scored on the named pulses, and the 12f→18f phase step is either reproduced within 30° on every judged window or shown not to come from the windings, screen or reactors. The bounded strays carry their identifiability. Negative control: with zero winding capacitance the replay reproduces the frequency-domain model's misses, step included. Results bearing on booster §14, §5 or §23 go to that plan's owner.

Amended 2026-10-16: the replay is scored, and the windings, screen and reactors are shown not to produce the 12f→18f step. What remains is the stray bounds. The frequency-domain and switched models miss 12f and 18f in opposite directions by up to about 20 dB, and both run high at 24f (§8), so a stray fitted to absolute line amplitudes would absorb that model-form error. The strays are therefore bounded from measured coil-to-coil transfer ratios at 6f–30f, starting with EF5→EF4 on E100318 (0.534 at 12f, against an inductive 0.288): a ratio between two coil voltages does not depend on how the source is modelled. The receiving coil's termination comes first. In E100318's replay window (−0.5 to 0.5 s) EF4's base reference is 0 and its base DC voltage about −1 V. Its coil current is 1.24 A rms while its terminal voltage carries 309 V rms of ripple. So at ripple frequencies EF4 is nearly open-circuit, and the 200 µH reactor into 0 V that the replay stamps for its idle supply clamps it to 0.000. At 731.4 Hz the OP2 plant's terminal impedance with EF4 open gives EF4/EF5 = 0.0647 with all 155 passive modes and 0.288 without them, so the passive conductors shield the coupling about fourfold. The switched open arm agrees, at 0.0655. The measured 0.534 exceeds the plant both with the passive modes and without them. Whatever carries it adds coupling beyond the coils' direct mutual inductance, or the plant over-shields at 12f, or both. The candidate paths into a floating EF4 are the passive conductors' resistance, which sets how strongly they shield; capacitive coupling (winding to winding, feeders, screen); and common-mode pickup through the grounding. They differ in how the ratio varies with frequency: shielding grows with frequency, capacitive coupling rises with it, and a common-mode path need not follow either. Done when a fragment tabulates, at each line from 6f to 30f on E100318's replay window, the measured EF5→EF4 ratio beside the plant's ratio with EF4 open, with and without the passive modes; gives, for each candidate path, the change it makes to that ratio across the path's physical range; and states which paths, alone or together, can reach the measured ratio at every line, and which the ratio's line-to-line shape excludes. Negative control: at 731.4 Hz the plant with EF4 open gives 0.0647 with all passive modes and 0.288 without them, each within 2 %; and a path whose effect on every line is below the ratio's window-to-window spread (about 5 % at 12f, §7) is reported as unconstrained.

§6 — The 2023 pulses, with the filter, the new grounding and the plasma

The 2023 restart added a ripple filter and a new grounding with design values, which is a controlled change in the stray network. The plasma pulses need a shot-matched equilibrium. None is held; it is asked for from the site (EQDB, a g-file or an IMAS equilibrium) in one bounded query, and nova takes it as a reconstructed plasma source (iter-passive-plasma-circuit §5). The section is held by gate g-jspr-2 on that source.

Done when the strays bounded from 2021, unchanged, predict the 2023 lines through the filter and the new grounding, scored as in §5. Negative control: the 2021 grounding in place of the 2023 one moves the predicted lines by the amount the design change implies.

§7 — One line estimator for the replay, and the EF5→EF4 transfer reconciled

§5's EF4-coupling node left four follow-ons on scripts/jt60sa/replay_2021.py and its tests. _line_amplitudes duplicates measurement.joint_line_coefficients (src/power_convertor/measurement.py:115) without that owner's folded-image (66−n) terms, although the owner is already imported and called in the same function. The record gives the measured EF5→EF4 12f transfer on E100318 as 0.534 through the acquisition chain, while coupling_transfer.json gives 0.560 at 732.6 Hz; the 4.7 % gap is unreconciled. The bare_indefinite and bare_condition flags carry no assertion. The carried-versus-imposed transfer test compares two generated JSON files under data/jt60sa/ef4_coupling and skips when they are absent, so it cannot fail on a code change.

Done when _line_amplitudes is removed and every caller reads lines through joint_line_coefficients; the replay's line results and the EF4 transfers are recomputed, and any change beyond 0.1 dB is tabulated; the fragment states which figure, 0.534 or 0.560, is the measured 12f transfer and why the other differs, with one measurement that shows it; a test asserts each conditioning flag on a constructed plant where it must hold and on one where it must not; and the transfer test recomputes both arms from the held E100318 trace rather than reading generated files. Negative control: the flag tests fail when each flag's comparison is inverted, and the replay's 6f agreement within 0.25 dB still holds after the change.

§8 — The frequency-domain and switched models on the same windows

The switched replay (§5) reproduces 6f within 0.25 dB on its windows of E100310 and E100318 (EF5) and E100321 and E100324 (EF2), where the measured 6f is 707–758 V, and over-predicts 12f by 2.3–6.1 dB, 18f by 6.9–9.5, 24f by 1.4–6.6 and 30f by 2.8–9.9. The frequency-domain booster model has not been scored on those windows. On the curated −3.5 to −1.0 s negative-current windows of the same four pulses (booster-converter-model §17, frozen arm), it reproduces 6f within 0.5 dB, under-predicts 12f by 3.6–6.9 dB (E100310 −3.59, E100318 −4.21, E100321 −6.77, E100324 −6.86) and over-predicts 24f by 6.7–11.4 dB (+11.39, +8.86, +6.68, +7.03); all fourteen of §17's negative-current windows share those signs. On its positive-current windows it over-predicts 12f to 24f. Whether the two models share a miss is therefore unknown, and it decides where to look: a miss both make points to what they share (the frozen 2021 parameters, the bridge overlap, the acquisition chain), and a miss only one makes points to where they differ (the switched bridge and base, the coupled plant).

Score both models through the same acquisition chain on the same windows: the replay's four windows, where the switched results already exist. Amended 2026-10-16: the switched model on §17's 2.5 s curated windows is not part of this section. Four such runs, one per pulse on separate CPU pairs, produced no result within 45 minutes each, because the solver runs at about 81 steps/s with about 1.8 switching events per step. They wait for a solver that checkpoints. Done when a fragment tabulates, per window and line from 6f to 30f, the two models' dB errors side by side, and classifies each line as a miss both models share, a miss of one model only, or agreement within the §1 band of filter-grounding-prediction. The frequency-domain model on the curated windows reproduces §17's frozen-arm line errors within 0.1 dB, and the replay on its own windows reproduces §5's within 0.1 dB. Negative control: with one model's predicted lines replaced by the measured lines on a window, every line that model missed reclassifies, a shared miss becoming a miss of the other model only and a one-model miss becoming agreement, and a classifier that leaves any of those lines unchanged fails. No 2023 shot is read, and src/power_convertor/fitted_parameters.py is unchanged.

§9 — Where the two models' 12f–30f predictions part

§8 shows the frequency-domain and switched models bracketing the measurement on the replay's four windows: on 12f and 18f they miss in opposite directions in every window, by up to about 20 dB between them. At 30f the two errors also have opposite signs, but in three of the four windows one of them lies inside the band. §2 found the switched bridges within 20 % of the analytic ones on the lines it checked, so most of the gap is expected in the transfer from source to coil terminal. The frequency-domain model carries a lumped loop, the booster's 3.25 mH in series with the coil and its couplings; the switched model carries the coupled plant (§4).

Split each model's predicted coil-voltage line, at each of 6f–30f on the four windows, into a source line and a source-to-coil transfer. The frequency-domain model's come from its own circuit. The switched model's source lines come from the switched units and its transfer from the plant's linear harmonic transfer, so no new switched simulation is run. Then score both models' base supply alone on base-only windows of EF2 and EF5 (booster-converter-model §15), where the base's firing angle is set by its recorded reference and no booster runs; that is the one case in which the source does not depend on the booster's firing law. Done when a fragment tabulates, per window and line, each model's source line and transfer and the share of the inter-model gap each accounts for; reports whether each model's source line times its transfer reproduces its §8 line within 0.5 dB, and by how much it does not where it does not; and states, from the base-only windows, which model's base prediction meets the §1 band of filter-grounding-prediction. Negative control: substituting one model's transfer into the other moves that model's line by the share the table assigns to the transfer, within 0.5 dB. No 2023 shot is read, and src/power_convertor/fitted_parameters.py is unchanged.

§10 — The switched lines split at each unit's loaded terminal

§9 found that the switched units' open-circuit source times the plant's linear transfer misses the switched coil lines by 3.5–32.6 dB, while on base-only windows both model forms' base supplies agree (12f in 11 of 11, 24f in 9 of 11). On booster windows the switched lines therefore depend on the converters' commutation under load, and the replay receipts do not keep each unit's loaded terminal voltage. Series units fired at different angles are the case this bears on: the base and booster here, and in ITER the sequentially controlled PF1 and PF6 pairs and the VS1 units in series on the PF2–PF5 node.

Rerun the replay on its four windows (E100310 and E100318 on EF5, E100321 and E100324 on EF2), recording every converter unit's terminal voltage through the same acquisition chain. Done when a fragment tabulates, per window and line from 6f to 30f, each unit's loaded terminal line, the plant's transfer from that terminal to the coil, and the summed product beside the switched coil line; and states, per line, whether the summed products reproduce the switched coil line within 0.5 dB and how much of the gap between the two model forms (§8) lies in the loaded unit sources and how much in the transfer. The rerun reproduces §8's switched coil lines within 0.1 dB. The same node carries two of §5's follow-ons: the check that §5's fragment matches the live plan moves into tests/test_jt60sa_replay_2021.py, and the tests pin §5's ratios at all five lines, not one 12f point. The third, folding open_receiver_transfer into src/power_convertor/loaded_pickup.py, waits until the coil-circuit plan's pickup-circuit node, which holds that file, has landed. Negative control: on a synthetic circuit with two series units of known sources and a known linear plant, the split recovers each unit's share within 0.1 dB, and with one unit's terminal tap removed the summed product departs from the coil line by that unit's share. No 2023 shot is read.

Measure narrowed before dispatch. The coil-circuit plan (S2) has since shown that its 12f EF5→EF4 transfer (0.557 and 0.560 against an M/L of 0.288) is not reproduced by any passive model. So harmonic lines cannot test the plant; that question is §5's, where the switched replay carries EF4 as a receiver. §4 is checked on what S2 validated: the slow coil-pair ratios at 0.1–30 Hz within its 4–8 % band, the self-inductances within 1–8 % of fast discharge, and agreement with S2's own nova-built plant to 1 % in terminal impedance. The negative control removes the passive structure. The 6f, 12f and 18f transfers the plant gives are reported as §5's baseline, not scored as §4's pass or fail. S2's EF5 positive control also confirms the plant on dumps: 18 pairs within 1.9–7.1 % rms of pickup peak.

§4 landed (merged dafded2): the OP2 plant through nova's call. It reproduces 8 of 9 measured slow coil-pair ratios, agrees with the coil-circuit plan's plant to 1.5e-4 to 5 kHz, and the harmonic transfers are recorded as §5's baseline. Gate g-jspr-1 is met. evidence

The OP2 plant's review follow-ons landed (merged 4f16d12) without changing the plant; the cached hashes are unchanged. The plant's coil block is the facility's pf_active matrix, forwarded as given. The independent check is now nova's own inductance computed from the machine's winding sections, which agrees with the facility matrix within 0.19–1.07 % per coil. That is a check on nova's kernels against JT-60SA's facility values, and the ITER plant relies on the same kernels. Three reviews: the first two blocked because the comparison read the plant's own input, and the third passed (goal 19 of 20). Open follow-on: no assertion pins the sign of the off-diagonal mutual inductances.

An input from the coil-circuit plan (S2), for this section to test. At the 12f line, EF5 drives EF4 at about twice its inductive M/L: nova's passive model predicts |H| = 0.065 against 0.568 measured, while the same geometry predicts eight of nine slow EF pairs within 4–8 % of M/L (jccm evidence, s5-nova). Something beyond the passive structure couples at the converter frequency. Two candidates are what this replay models and the frequency-domain model does not. One is capacitive coupling through the windings, busbars and feeders. The other is a common-mode path through the grounding: in ITER's PF2–PF5 circuit a shared return branch moves the grounded midpoint by half its voltage (ITER_D_22HXXE eq. 3.03c). So the 2021 replay should carry EF4 as a receiving circuit, its supply connected and idle, and report the switched model's EF5→EF4 transfer at 12f beside the measured 0.568. The winding result of §3 already argues against a winding resonance as the cause.

First replay landed as a negative result (merged 4242c6b). E100310 and E100318 on EF5, E100321 and E100324 on EF2 were scored 6f–30f through the acquisition chain. 6f agrees within 0.25 dB on every pulse. 12f is over-predicted by 2.3–6.1 dB, 18f by 6.9–9.5, 24f by 1.4–6.6 and 30f by 2.8–9.9. The 12f→18f phase step is not reproduced (about 90° off on E100310). Removing the winding terminal capacitance moves no line by more than 0.08 dB, so the capacitance is inert at these lines and reproduces the frequency-domain model's misses. E100303 shows no booster lines to anchor on, as expected of a base-only control. The plant-equivalence precondition fails (driven coils 0.4–11 %, EF6 worst; the undriven FPPC pair 28 and 97 V) and does not shrink with the step. jt60sa-plant-equivalence is now settling it against an inversion-free reference, because the replay's averaged-route voltages pass through a pseudo-inverse. The first attempt's slowness was thread oversubscription; capped, the solver runs about 550 steps/s. Still owed: the EF5→EF4 transfer at 12f and the bounded strays, after equivalence.

Plant equivalence settled (merged 86b617b). The adapter was not at fault. The replay's averaged-route reference started its passive state at zero, where the state consistent with the imposed currents is −M·i(0). Seeded correctly, the averaged route agrees with an inversion-free reference built from the plant's own fields to 8.8e-6 of peak. The switched route agrees to 0.48 % at a 5 µs step; its error is first order in the step, 1.7 % at the replay's 20 µs. OP2's winding block is positive definite (condition 110); ITER's is singular only through VS1's shared return, which the adapter's pseudo-inverse already handles. The 6f–30f line results stand: the step error is about 0.15 dB against misses of 2–10 dB. jt60sa-ef4-coupling is now running. It carries EF4 as a circuit with its supply idle, and runs one ablation per path to find what lifts the 12f transfer from the inductive 0.288 to the measured 0.56. It also bounds the strays below 2 kHz and checks the results at 5 µs.

EF5→EF4 coupling landed (merged 7ff5b58). On E100318 the 12f transfer measured through the acquisition chain is 0.534; coupling_transfer.json gives 0.560, a gap not yet reconciled. The inductive M/L is 0.288. EF4 was carried as a circuit, one path at a time: inductive only 0.066; with winding capacitance 0.107; with grounding 0.027; with the switched idle supply 0.000; all paths together 0.000. Imposed on its measured current, EF4 gives 0.234 (0.285 against the measured EF5 voltage), which recovers the inductive transfer and nothing beyond it. No path at EF4's terminals carries the excess. It needs EF4's own current to be about 1.9 times what induction drives. A resonance below 12f would need about 89 nF, 2.5 times the winding-capacitance budget, and is not proposed. Open: the idle supply, stamped as a 200 µH reactor into a 0 V source, clamps EF4 to 0.01 V, so its model may be too stiff. The review's follow-ons pass to this plan's owner: _line_amplitudes duplicates measurement.joint_line_coefficients without the folded-image terms, the 0.534/0.560 gap, unguarded conditioning flags, and an artefact-only transfer test. The power_convertor ITER coordinator no longer dispatches JT-60SA characterisation. Remaining work for this plan's owner: §6 (2023 pulses), the stray bounds, and the 12f–30f over-prediction.

[Independent EF4 stray-bounds review](/home/ITER/mcintos/.config/reckon/crew/reviews/power_convertor/r-20261016T123915144125-jspr-stray-bounds.at-3b1f7e63d95ab5e8de6e5d17c733f1556436c16b.json) records six scores, one blocking source-contract mismatch and three follow-on findings at the exact reviewed revision.

§5 closed. The replay was scored on its four 2021 windows and the 12f–18f phase step is shown not to come from the windings, screen or reactors. The strays are bounded at merge 9e03938: EF4 is nearly open at ripple frequencies; the plant gives 0.0647 with its passive modes and 0.288 without, against 0.534 measured.
